courses.title: Shema across the canon
courses.description: Six sessions from Torah declaration to Gemara reasoning.

sessions.title: Hear the address
sessions.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
sessions.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
choices: The people Israel, addressed together as one.
The individual worshipper reciting the line in prayer.
God, addressed in the second person of praise.
sessions.explanation: Start with the source's own voice before its later uses — the verse addresses Israel, not the reciter or God.

sessions.title: Read the scope
sessions.hebrew: ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך
sessions.translation: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, being, and might.
sessions.prompt: What does the repeated ‘with all’ language do?
choices: It expands the command to reach the whole person.
It fixes the times at which love must be shown.
It records a disagreement between two schools.
sessions.explanation: Repetition and expansion are literary evidence — the threefold ‘with all’ widens the command, it does not schedule or dispute it.

sessions.title: Carry words into life
sessions.hebrew: והיו הדברים האלה על לבבך ושננתם לבניך ודברת בם
sessions.translation: These words shall be upon your heart; teach them diligently and speak of them.
sessions.prompt: What movement does the passage make?
choices: From inward attention outward to teaching and speech.
From a stated ruling to the objection against it.
From the land of exile back toward return.
sessions.explanation: The source connects heart, teaching, and recurring speech — an inward-to-outward movement, not a legal dispute or an exile narrative.

sessions.title: Meet the Siddur
sessions.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
sessions.translation: The Torah line becomes recurring communal recitation.
sessions.prompt: What does the liturgical setting add?
choices: A recurring communal function the verse did not state alone.
A replacement that lets prayer stand in for the Torah source.
A binding ruling on exactly when the words must be said.
sessions.explanation: Later use adds a role without erasing the original source — it neither replaces the verse nor legislates its timing.

sessions.title: Ask the Mishnah's question
sessions.translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
sessions.prompt: What kind of question is this?
choices: A practical question about the boundary of a time.
A philosophical question defining what prayer is.
A historical question about when the practice began.
sessions.explanation: The Mishnah receives a known practice through a precise case — asking from-when is a timing boundary, not a definition or a date.

sessions.title: Explain the Gemara's pressure
sessions.translation: On what is the tanna standing, that he teaches ‘from when?’
choices: The unstated context the Mishnah assumes but never states.
A new prayer text introduced to replace the Mishnah's.
The final conclusion the discussion has already reached.
sessions.explanation: The learner can now follow a Torah line through prayer, practice, and argument — the Gemara probes the Mishnah's assumed context, not a new text or a settled conclusion.

production.prompt: You met these two words in Session 1 and again in the Siddur. Type their English meaning from memory.

courses.title: Blessings as a source chain
courses.description: Six sessions from receiving a gift to studying its legal reception.

sessions.title: Read the sequence
sessions.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.
choices: Eating, then satisfaction, then blessing.
Blessing first, then eating, then satisfaction.
A question, then an objection, then a resolution.
sessions.explanation: The verse supplies an ordered source for later study — eat, be satisfied, then bless, in that order.

sessions.title: Name the object of gratitude
sessions.hebrew: על הארץ הטבה אשר נתן לך
sessions.translation: For the good land that He has given you.
sessions.prompt: What does the verse join to blessing?
choices: A concrete gift received, and the One who gave it.
A precise legal measurement of how much was eaten.
A specific historical period in the nation's past.
sessions.explanation: The verse frames blessing as response to received goodness — a gift and its giver, not a measurement or a date.

sessions.title: See a communal form
sessions.translation: Three who ate together join in an invitation to bless.
choices: A communal threshold and a shared form of blessing.
A new Torah verse not cited anywhere before it.
A philosophical proof that blessing is obligatory.
sessions.explanation: A later source can specify how a theme enters shared practice — here a threshold of three and a communal form, not a verse or a proof.

sessions.title: Ask what Gemara adds
sessions.hebrew: כל הנהנה מן העולם הזה בלא ברכה
sessions.translation: Whoever benefits from this world without a blessing…
sessions.prompt: What should a reader ask next?
choices: What claim or pressure this statement adds to the practice.
Which single word in the line is easiest to memorize.
Why the surrounding context can safely be ignored here.
sessions.explanation: Gemara reading asks what work a statement performs — not which word to memorize, and never to ignore context.

sessions.title: Keep the boundary
choices: The difference between studying law and issuing a ruling.
A shortcut that lets a learner skip past the sources.
A reason to avoid engaging with practice altogether.
sessions.explanation: Seder teaches source literacy, not personal psak — the sequence guards the study/ruling line, it is not a shortcut or an excuse to disengage.

sessions.title: State the chain
sessions.prompt: Which account best maps the unit?
choices: A Torah response becomes communal practice and later reasoning.
Each later source erases and replaces the one before it.
Only the earliest source carries any real weight.
sessions.explanation: You can now trace a source across genres while preserving their differences — the layers build, they do not erase or outrank one another.

production.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.
production.prompt: This phrase opened the course. Type its English meaning from memory, in a few words.
acceptable: you shall eat be satisfied and bless
you will eat be satisfied and bless
you shall eat and be satisfied and bless
and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless
